name: Battle_AutoAction_Step
summary: Per-frame step of the auto-battle action sequencer: waits until the current battle actor is idle, then plays the queued message/popup pair for the acting unit and advances the state in self+0x6E34 (0x2C6D..0x2CA3), returning true when the step completed.
evidence: The now-named caller Battle_AutoAction_Update calls it exactly where its state machine enters the 0x2D19/0x2CCC states and only advances when this returns non-zero; it uses the same self+0x6E34 state word and the same battle-work +0x4320 actor check as that caller.

name: Battle_AutoAction_Precheck
summary: Validates that every party member can act before the auto-battle list is built: for each member it rejects unusable/unselectable states and too-low stats, then fires the pending item actions of record type 2 and sets the refresh byte self+0x6E3C when the two equipped item name keys differ.
evidence: Its only caller Battle_AutoAction_Update invokes it on the sequencer's -1 entry state, right before it fills the action list, and aborts when the result is 0; the body walks the same party member count (func_00630DC8) and item table (func_0063FD24) as that caller.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote
signature: u32 Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote(void* player, int restart, u32* outSlots, u32 expectedId)
summary: Starts one sequence note across up to eight voices: allocates the voice slots from the mixer, starts them at priority 0x7FFF, queues one stream read per slot and then applies the per-channel output-mode/loop flags.
evidence: Sound_Command_ExecuteList (the sequence-command dispatcher) passes the command operands straight in: command[4]=player, command[5]=restart, command+6=slot array, command[0xE]=expected note id, and the body's guard compares that id with player+0x21F8; the only damaged register in the readable C (unaff_r7) is explicitly set to 0x7FFF, the voice priority.

name: maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_UpdateActiveNotes
signature: void maybe_Sound_SeqPlayer_UpdateActiveNotes(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 frame, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Consumes the sequence player's active note table: loops the entries in the 'ready' state (state byte 3 at +0x241), accumulates their sample offsets into f_58, requeues stream work through Sound_Stream_QueueWorkItem and starts the next batch of voices.
evidence: No other function refers to it by name, so the role still rests on the body: it is the note-table consumer using the same Sound_Stream_QueueWorkItem / voice-loop layout as the confirmed Sound_SeqPlayer_StartMultiVoiceNote family. The body also contains an unaff_r5 (damaged VFP/flag register), so it stays maybe_.

name: std_ThrowWideRange

summary: Throws/format-checks a UTF-16 range for the basic_string<wchar_t> layer: builds the two-byte-stride range end (msg + len*2 - 2) and returns the formatted length or 0xFFFFFFFF when the range did not fit.
evidence: All 18 call sites are the std_WString format constructors (maybe_std_WString_FormatCtorA..G and std_WString_FormatInitA..E) calling it as std_ThrowWideRange(out + 1, capacity, ...), i.e. the same wide-string range primitive; the 16-bit stride in the body matches the wchar_t buffer those ctors build.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_SetModelAndPos
signature: void Gfx_SpriteActor_SetModelAndPos(SpriteActor* self, const void* params, u32 modelId, u32 variant)
summary: Applies the sprite model selected by (modelId, variant) to a 2D actor: creates the table entry, stores its anim id and the ids on the scene node, applies the priority byte, sets the model size from the locator param block and starts the idle animation.
evidence: Both callers are the warp locators Actor2DWarpLocator and ActorWarpToMapJumpLocatorID, which pass a locator param block plus the model/variant fields of the destination entry; the named callees (Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize, Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation) confirm the 'apply model + placement/animation' role.

summary: Third 2D sprite-actor initialiser: copies the param block (position, size, model/variant, flags), creates the collision and effect sprites, and then scans the per-map variant list at params->f_28 (entries stride 0x18) for the first entry whose area flag (+0x17) is satisfied by work+0xF14+0x27508, storing the chosen variant in f_240/f_242/f_2A8.
evidence: Same family as the confirmed Field_CreateCollisionSprite/Field_CreateEffectSprite initialisers and it calls Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable with params->f_28/f_26, but no caller names it and the 'C' ordinal only says which param layout it uses, so it stays maybe_.

summary: Prepares the scene flow's 0x80-byte sprite context once (lazy allocation through func_00384050), then returns 0 while the step helper reports it is still running and 1 when the ready flag at step+8 is clear.

name: Ui_Window_ResetSubObjectLists
summary: Re-initialises the window's two intrusive child lists at +0x134 and +0x198 after a sub-object id change: unlinks the current entries, resets both heads to their sentinels, then loads the data-manager sub-object for the id (or the default one through Ui_TutorialPane_ShowEntry).

name: Field_Actor_UpdateCellTransition
summary: Moves the player actor across a map-cell boundary: bails out while the game-work mode bytes or the UI transition are busy, compares the cell computed from the actor grid position (+0x78/+0x7C) with the cached cell, then either performs the cell switch (release trail, redraw, idle animation) or offsets the actor position by the cell delta.
evidence: The named callees in both branches (maybe_Field_Actor_ComputeCellTransitionOffset, Gfx_Trail_Smooth, Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState, Ui_ObjectList_Begin/End) plus the position writes confirm the per-frame cell-transition step; only its caller is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcBaseStatDamage
summary: Computes a damage-scale figure for one battle unit: rejects the unit by state/type, reads its party member stats (func_0035EB98 +0x742/+0xEC2/+0xB02) and the attacker/monster records, clamps the middle term to 0..40 and returns whether the resulting 0.01-scaled product reaches 1%.

name: Battle_Message_RowIsActive
summary: Decides whether the optional battle-message row (type 0x75 or 0x11B) is shown: checks the row type, verifies the member's equipped item record flag, then rolls the battle RNG in [1,100] and compares it with the row's random threshold.
evidence: Its named caller Battle_Message_BuildActorRowBig stores the result as a row-active flag, and the body's RNG roll (func_001CA474) against the row's +0x?? threshold matches the name; the earlier 'Message_' family is confirmed as battle message rows, not text metrics.

name: Battle_Monster_RefreshConditionFlags
summary: Re-rolls the condition row values (0x3A/0x3B/0x3C plus 0xB5/0x100) of a battle monster: for each row it checks whether either equipped item's record type is 0x0B/0x10/0x12 and refreshes the row value when one matches.

name: Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionIconAlpha
signature: void Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionIconAlpha(int* self, u32 rowId, int force)

name: Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionRow
signature: void Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionRow(int effectId, int memberIndex, int targetUnit, u32 flags, int arg5)

summary: Rolls a weighted scene-object state: looks up tableRecId in the field tables (0x0063E6C4/0x0063E70C), filters up to 16 candidates by the active scene mask (1 << 0x0066A764), picks one with Math_WeightedRandomIndexDefaultRng, registers its timer (u8_02 * 60) in gameWork+0x24A98 and writes the 12-byte result.

The body still shows unaff_r7/r8 (Ghidra dropped the high halves of the 12-byte return); the file header records that the full ARM disassembly 0x15CDC4..0x15D048 was recovered, so the two unaff_ registers are a decompiler artefact of a damaged return, not a different function.

signature: unsigned char Menu_TestEntryCondition(MenuState* self, int entryTable, int index)
summary: Tests the per-entry condition byte at entryTable+0x205+index*2: case 1/2 compare the actor's HP/MP ratio with the threshold, case 3 tests a status bit, later cases count party members, and it returns whether the entry is usable.
evidence: Two named callers (Menu_SelectRecipeRow, Menu_UpdateSelectionPage) use the result to grey out/refuse entry rows, and the body's HP/MP/party-count branches match a usability condition test.

name: Field_ActorAction_Ctor
signature: void* Field_ActorAction_Ctor(u32 arg1, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Base constructor of the field actor-action objects: forwards the five arguments to the generic object factory with flags 0x20000001, installs the shared action vtable and stores the second argument at +0x28.
evidence: Five named field action creators (Field_CreateActionHorseInput, Field_CreateActionHorseStart, Field_CreateActionMoveStep, Field_CreateActionRun, maybe_Field_CreateActionNut) call it as their first step, so it is the common action base constructor.

name: Gfx_SpriteObject_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a 2D sprite/particle object: allocates it with tag 0x20000001, installs vtable 0x002357D8 and seeds the position/velocity/scale/uv blocks from the shared constant tables at 0x002357DC..0x002357E0.
evidence: The body is fully readable (vtable literal, three 8-word default blocks, -0x800 sentinels), which makes the constructor role certain; there is no caller to fix the owning class beyond 'sprite object'.

name: maybe_BattleAi_BuildCandidateAction
signature: int maybe_BattleAi_BuildCandidateAction(BattleAiContext* self, u32 index, u32 category, int listBase, int** outList)
summary: Battle-AI candidate scoring step: rolls candidate weights, builds the message/estimation rows for a party member (Text_BuildRowForMember, Battle_Message_ApplyRowLayout) and returns the action kind of the winning candidate (4 skill, 5 spell, 6 item).
evidence: FACTS.md marks 0x00269F64..0x00277700 as BattleAi_* (AI action evaluator) - the old 'Ui_TextLayout_...' prefix was from the poisoned range - and both its caller (BattleAi_SelectBestCandidateFromAllCategories) and its callees (BattleAi_RollCandidateWeight, BattleAi_AppendCandidateFromSkill, Battle_Message_ApplyRowLayout) are BattleAi; the return codes 4/5/6 are the action-kind codes documented in FACTS, but the body is damaged (unaff_r5, halt_baddata) so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateEffectsC
summary: Slot 15 of the battle member-widget vtable: computes the member's effect transform, creates the scaled effect 0x450, plays the member's effect SE and, when the record has an effect id at +0x92, creates the keyed effect instance and stores the handle at self[0x49E].
evidence: The body matches the other member-widget effect slots (same self[0x49D]/self[0x49E] handles and Effect_CreateScaledInstance/Effect_FindOrCreateInstance), but the slot is only reached through the vtable and no caller names it.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateEffects
summary: Effect update for the member widget: resolves the effect handles for the member's slots, places the marker through 0x00572C50 and stores the resulting handle.
evidence: Four named callers (Battle_ActionSequence_Update, Battle_Actor_Update) pass the sequence plus member/slot ids and use the returned handle, and Svc_ResolveObjectHandle / Effect_FindOrCreateInstance are named callees.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_Init
summary: Initialises an actor action from the actor: clears state, snapshots the actor transform into f_54 and copies the bone/attachment transform blocks (+0x5F4 of the current part, default 0x007E7110) into f_78..f_A4.
evidence: The structure is visible (transform snapshot + attachment block copies), but the action family is unknown and its only caller is maybe_Field_ActorAction_StopTurn.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_PlayStateEffect
signature: void maybe_Field_Object2D_PlayStateEffect(Field_Object2D* self, int state, u32 arg3, float arg4)
summary: Starts the effect that belongs to a given object state: for states 10/11 it stops the previous effect, builds the spawn transform from the object position and requests effect id 0x4B5, also notifying the model interface through vtable +0x38.
evidence: The literal 0x4B5 and the state switch are clear and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance/Effect_ReleaseHandle are named, but nothing calls it yet, so the class attribution stays tentative.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_BeginEffectState
summary: Switches an actor's effect state: if the byte at +0x238 is not 0xFF it clears +0x221, builds an effect transform at the actor position and spawns effect 0x45C through the 2D effect manager, then sets f_8C=1 and stops the sub-animation; otherwise it plays animation 0x0032DD6C and clears f_8C.
evidence: The spawner is now named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and the two branches are readable, but no caller confirms the 'begin effect state' semantics.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpawnScreenShake
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SpawnScreenShake(void* source, int id, float amount)
summary: Spawns a screen-shake/effect instance from a source transform: reads the position, computes a length and forwards the request to Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: The readable file has no doc header (recovered entry point only) and the body is a short transform-length + Effect_FindOrCreateInstance call; no caller identifies it as a screen shake specifically.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_PlaySituationEffect
summary: Plays one of five situation effects keyed by the actor type byte at +0x2E5: builds the effect parameter block from the actor position, creates the effect through the effect manager at uiCore+0x60 and sets the +0xB2 busy flag.
evidence: The callee is now named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance and its two callers (maybe_Field_Actor_TriggerNearbySameType) use the result as a started-effect flag, but the caller itself is a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowNextPageWithControls
summary: Shows the next page of a message: releases the current page elements, emits the control codes 0x2E..0x3B that build the page header/footer and then pushes the first control byte of the page.
evidence: Named callees Ui_Root_ReleaseAll, Ui_MessageWindow_ExecControlCode, Ui_MessageWindow_ExecNextControlByte and the 0x2E..0x3B code constants support the page-with-controls reading, but no caller exists and the body has a bad-instruction block.

name: maybe_Ui_TextWindow_RefreshLine
summary: Refreshes the current line: in an active message state it emits the next control byte when the read and write cursors (f_1948/f_194C) differ, otherwise it clears the line with the empty string.
evidence: Ui_MessageWindow_ExecNextControlByte is the confident callee and the cursor comparison is explicit, but the function has no caller and its tail is wcslen (0x00100B74).

name: Battle_Ui_CollectActionTargets
summary: Collects the distinct actor pointers referenced by the queued actions into a local vector and pushes the resulting target set to the UI as popup number/actor lists.
evidence: Four named battle-update callers (Battle_ActionSequence_Update_2, Battle_Sequence_Update, Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_Update/B) pass their battle object, and the body de-duplicates action-slot actors before Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNumberList/SpawnForActorList.

name: Ui_SmithMenu_UpdateDetailList
summary: Refreshes the smith menu's detail list from the controller: for cell index 1 only it takes the controller's current entry and row count, then pushes both into the detail list widget through Ui_SmithMenu_SetDetailPair; other cell indices push a null entry.
evidence: Four named smith-menu callers (Ui_SmithMenu_CommitRow, Ui_SmithMenu_HandleCommand, Ui_SmithMenu_HandleListInput, Ui_SmithMenu_SelectRow) pass the row/input controller, and the body is gated on the named Ui_SmithMenu_GetCellIndex.

name: Ui_Widget_SetChildVisible
summary: Forwards a boolean to the widget's sub-object at +0x128: func_0029126C stores it as the object's +0x14 flag and mirrors bit 0 into the child's +0x44 visible bit.
evidence: The three callers (Ui_SmithMenu_HandleListInput, maybe_Ui_ListWindow_HandleDetailToggle, maybe_Ui_Part_SetupFromActorSprite) always pass 0 to hide a detail child, and the disassembly of func_0029126C confirms the +0x44 visible-bit mirroring.

name: maybe_Camera_TestPointOccluded
signature: int maybe_Camera_TestPointOccluded(InteractRequest* request, const unsigned char* rgb)
summary: Projects a field point with the camera helper and asks the camera system whether that point is hidden by an occluder; the request's virtual validator and the object table then confirm the hit.
evidence: Its three callers are all named hit-test paths (Field_BattleTrigger_Update, Field_BattleTrigger_HandleTouch, maybe_Field_CheckGridInteraction) that pass the trigger plus its +0x48 colour block, but some callee names in this range are themselves questionable, so 'occluded' stays an inference.

name: maybe_Font_GetAtlasCellForChar
summary: Resolves the font-atlas cell of the character stored in the text row: maps the glyph's atlas coordinates (f_78/f_7C, scaled by 8) through Font_Atlas_LookupCell, binds the cell and returns the glyph metric at +0x16.
evidence: Font_Atlas_LookupCell is a confident callee and the body only maps glyph coordinates and metrics, but there is no caller and the row class is inferred; the function does not resolve item rows even though it reads a data-manager table.

name: maybe_Field_CheckGridInteraction
summary: Resolves the grid cell under the player, classifies the four neighbouring direction entries of the cell table against the current map-object tables and then asks the camera-interaction test (0x00651954) to confirm the hit.
evidence: Both callers (maybe_Field_TryPlayerInteractGated, maybe_Field_TryPlayerInteract) are interaction attempts, and the callee 0x00651954 is the point hit test; both are maybe_ themselves, so the wording stays tentative.

name: Battle_ApplyMonsterEffect
signature: void Battle_ApplyMonsterEffect(u32 effectId, BattleWork* work, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int arg5)
summary: Loads the display rows for a monster's effect/condition: with a concrete effect id it formats the effect text and loads the condition record by the record's type (4/8/other); with 0xFF it instead takes the member's equipped item, switches on its category and refreshes the matching condition rows.
evidence: Its caller Battle_CalcDefenseReduction passes the effect id, and the named callees maybe_Monster_FormatEffectText / maybe_Battle_Monster_LoadConditionRecord plus Item_LookupRecord fix the effect-row loading.

name: Battle_UnitModel_SetVariantPaired
summary: Switches the unit-model object to the variant used when a partner unit is present: sets f_142=0/f_143=1, resolves model id 0x18F, builds its animation instance and attaches it through the f_13C slot.
evidence: The caller BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant calls this and its Solo twin 0x004A8084 according to the partner flag, and the two bodies are identical except for the flags and attachment slot.

name: Battle_UnitModel_SetVariantSolo
summary: Switches the unit-model object to the variant used when no partner unit is present: sets f_142=1/f_143=0, resolves model id 0x18F, builds its animation instance and attaches it through the f_138 slot.
evidence: Same body as 0x004A7E58 with the opposite flags and the other attachment slot; BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant picks between the two on the partner flag.

name: Battle_UnitModelB_SetVariantPaired
summary: Second unit-model class (model id 0x1A5) switching to its partner-present variant: sets f_142=0/f_143=1, resolves model 0x1A5, builds the animation instance with mode 0 and attaches it through the f_13C slot.
evidence: The vtable 0x775AB8 and slot A8 are explicit and the body is the exact sibling of 0x004A7E58 with only the model id and modes changed.

name: Battle_UnitModelB_SetVariantSolo
summary: Second unit-model class switching to its partner-absent variant: sets f_142=1/f_143=0, resolves model 0x1A5, builds the animation instance with mode 0 and attaches it through the f_138 slot.
evidence: Mirror of 0x004A8084 with model id 0x1A5/mode 0 and vtable slot A4; the family relation and the flag split are explicit in the two sibling bodies.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_OnEventEffect
signature: void maybe_Field_SceneObject_OnEventEffect(Field_SceneObject* self, int eventId, void* arg3)
summary: Event virtual of a field scene object that forwards the event to its children and then handles the gimmick effect: 0x10 resets the effect/animation state, 0xA spawns effect 0x496 at the object position +0.3 in Y and 0xB releases it.
evidence: The event switch and the named Effect_CreateScaledInstance/Effect_ReleaseHandle calls are readable, but there is no caller and the slot is only known from the vtable.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ApplySpeakerGauge
summary: Refreshes the message window's speaker state: finds the party member whose gauge the window is showing, clamps the window value against that member's remaining value, applies the speaker's two text colours and then either closes the animation or plays UI animation 0x27->0x28.
evidence: The named neighbours Ui_ApplyTextColor/Ui_ApplyTextColorAlt and Message_SetArg confirm the speaker/text-colour part, but the 'gauge' half has no caller to confirm it.

name: Field_SceneObject_HandleResetEvent
summary: Event-0x10 handler body: hides the fixed model slots, releases the stored effect handle f_2FC, respawns the scaled effect f_300 at the object position and resets the animation-slot table f_2C8..f_2E4.
evidence: Its named caller Field_SceneObject_OnEvent calls it exactly for event id 0x10, and the body's Model_AttachSlot_HideAll + Effect_ReleaseHandle + Effect_CreateScaledInstance sequence matches a reset handler.

name: Regex_NodeAlloc
signature: void Regex_NodeAlloc(u32* out, RegexNodeList* list, int node)
summary: Allocates a list node (two units from the regex allocator 0x00514390), sets the self-referencing list pointers and inserts it after the list head, then stores the caller's value word.
evidence: Seven named Regex_Op* handlers (Regex_OpBuildOperandSets, Regex_OpPushValueAndVariants, Regex_OpPushNamedClass, ...) call it to append a result node, which fixes both the allocator and the list-insert semantics.

name: Ui_ScreenTransition_IsBlockingDraw
summary: Returns 1 if self->f_DC is non-null and its vt[+0x0C]() returns 0, if any of the five overlay/fade layers (+0xE0, +0xE4, +0x110, +0xF8, +0x10C) has active byte +0x94 != 0, or if self->u32_114 != 0; returns 0 only when all are clear.
evidence: Ten named callers in the field renderer (Field2D_Scene_RenderAll, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects, Field2D_Sprite_UpdateState, Field2D_MapChip_WalkTrace, Battle_TextWindow_UpdateVisibility*) gate drawing on the result, and the disassembly 0x632FC4..0x633060 strictly returns 0/1.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep
signature: int maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep(Field2DSprite* sprite, const short* step, int arg3)
summary: Chooses the next path step for a field-2D sprite: tests the target box overlap against the sprite position plus the step vector, then picks a random +/- extent from the sprite's 0x2B4 record and clamps it into the bounds.
evidence: The overlap tests and Math_RandRangeInt(0,2) are visible and five callers use the boolean result to advance, but large parts of the body are unrecoverable (halt_baddata, SBORROW4, a bogus func_0xffda23fe).

name: Battle_Action_SelectEffectTarget
signature: u32 Battle_Action_SelectEffectTarget(void* action, u32* units, int unitCount, u32 mask)
summary: Scans the candidate target units of an action (array + count) and returns the best matching target handle: it filters by the action's flag mask, checks the field condition/group reference against the acting actor's scenario id and compares the effect transforms through maybe_Battle_ComputeEffectTransform, preferring the lowest record +0x60.
evidence: Five callers pass an action plus its unit array/count and a mask constant (8, 0x40, 0x10, 4), and the named callees Field_Condition_HasActiveRef / Field_Object_HasActiveGroupRef / Field_SceneNode_GetPosition match the filtering described. The flagged unaff_r11 is assigned from the loop variable iVar6 before use, so it is a register artefact rather than damaged data.

name: maybe_Battle_CanUseItemOnSelf
summary: Item acceptance test used by the equipment/item panels: looks up the item record and returns 1 only when the item's kind byte +0x11 is not '#' or when the manager lookup succeeds, with item 0x9E0 whitelisted.
evidence: Its three callers are all named item-panel refreshes (Ui_EquipmentWindow_OpenItemPage, Ui_EquipRow_Refresh, Ui_ItemPanel_RefreshFromConditions) passing the UI manager and an item id, which supports an item usability test; several callee names in this body are themselves doubtful, so the exact rule stays uncertain.

name: maybe_Snd_StreamVoice_UpdateFragment
summary: Ghidra mis-split: this entry is the tail of the ARM streamed-voice routine 0x00105584, so the C shown is the stop/fade/async-transfer part of that routine rather than an independent function.
evidence: The address sits inside ARM code exactly at the end of 0x00105584 (the ARM twin 0x00105AFC follows it), the body starts mid-state-machine and contains coprocessor_movefromRt, and no caller exists.

name: Script_Registry_BuildDelegateTable
summary: Builds a Squirrel registry/class table from a static spec array: allocates 0x48-byte nodes, initialises them from the 24-byte spec triples, copies the literal names and links them into the hash table (Sq_HashTable_Init/Sq_HashTable_Set).
evidence: All ten call sites are Script_Vm_RegisterDefaultDelegates passing the VM plus a static spec table (0x007AFA18, 0x007AFAA8, ...), and the body calls Sq_HashTable_Init/Set and Script_Registry_LinkObject; the old 'Text_FormatBuildSegments' name was wrong (no formatter is involved).

name: maybe_Ui_PartyMember_ShowValueChange
summary: Item-use result pane for a party member: opens with the same layout as 0x004C4868 (dead-member branch pushes the pane and sets cells 3/0x30) and then shows the member's changed value through the item-use panes.
evidence: The body shares the item-use callees (Item_LookupRecord, func_0035EB98, Ui_Window_PushPane, Item_RollStatBoostDelta, Ui_ItemUse_ConsumeSourceItem) with 0x004C4868, but the opening alone cannot distinguish HP from MP/stat items and there is no caller.

name: maybe_Ui_FieldMessageWindow_Init
summary: Opens the field message sub-window: picks the pane layout from the current message/scene state, pushes the panes and queues the events that drive the window.
evidence: The named Ui_Window_PushPane and Ui_Panel_ResetAndPush callees fit 'open the window', but the body also calls item-use helpers and there is no caller, so the class attribution is weak.

name: Ui_ItemUse_ApplyHpRecovery
summary: Applies an HP-recovery item to a party member and shows the result: rolls the boost (Item_RollStatBoostDelta), adds it to the member's HP at +0x14 clamped to max HP (vt[+8]), consumes the item and pushes the matching recovery/full/revive pane (cells 1/2/3/4/9/0x30).
evidence: The body reads member+0x14 (HP per FACTS.md) and the vt[+8] max-HP getter, calls Item_RollStatBoostDelta and Ui_ItemUse_ConsumeSourceItem, and the branches set the 'recovered' vs 'already full' vs 'revived' panes; the old 'ShowValueGain' wording was too vague.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowEntry
summary: Item-use result pane for a party member and the row's item: when the member's +0xDA bit 1 is set it pushes a pane, sets cells 1/9 and clears the equip mark.
evidence: The body uses the same item-use helpers (Item_LookupRecord, func_0035EB98, Ui_Window_PushPane, Ui_ItemUse_ConsumeSourceItem) as 0x004C4868 but gates on the member's +0xDA flag bit; there is no caller, so the 'message window entry' wording is unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_FieldMessageWindow_InitB
summary: Place-dependent window open: if the current place id is 1 it sets menu mode 1, pushes the first pane descriptor and plays steps 0x0F/0x11; otherwise it pushes the alternate descriptor, plays 0x0F/0x10 and, when the record lookup succeeds, hands self+0x14 to the panel and resets/pushes it.
evidence: The branch condition is the named maybe_Field_GetCurrentPlaceId and the sibling call maybe_Ui_Menu_SetMode, but no caller and no class name confirm the field-message window.

name: Item_CanAddOneMore
summary: For the item in a member inventory cell (+0xEC): reads the per-item stack limit (+0x45) and returns whether the held count plus one stays within it.
evidence: The body resolves the cell's item with Item_LookupRecord, reads the limit byte +0x45 and the bag count, and its named caller Ui_ItemUse_ConsumeSourceItem uses it to decide whether the consumed item can be added back.
